name: Housing.com
tagline: Indian property portal for buying, renting and selling homes, with paid visibility plans for owners, brokers and builders.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Free for seekers, paid listing and visibility packages for owners, agents and developers.

verdictSummary: Housing.com is not an app, it is an inventory pile with a search box on top. The thing you actually want is the listings: lakhs of live flats, owner phone numbers, builder project pages, and the brokers who keep refreshing them because that is where the buyers are. An agent can clone the UI in an afternoon and it will be an empty UI. There is no legal, stable firehose of Indian property listings you can point a personal build at, and scraping it gets you blocked, stale, or both. What you can build is the layer the portal is genuinely bad at: a private tracker for the twenty flats you are actually considering.
coreLoopDIY: A local app where you paste listing URLs or details, and it dedupes them, scores each on rent per square foot, commute and your own weights, pins them on a map, and tracks visits and follow-ups.
requirements: Listings you find yourself, pasted in manually or via a saved-search email forward
Internet access for geocoding via a public OpenStreetMap endpoint
A browser, no accounts, no cloud
whatYouLose: The actual listing inventory, which is the entire product
Owner and broker contact details you cannot get anywhere else
New listings appearing within minutes of being posted
Builder project pages, floor plans, RERA details and price trend data
Mobile app, alerts, and the chat and callback plumbing that makes sellers respond
moatNotes: Two-sided and local: sellers list where buyers search, buyers search where listings are, and both are city by city. A personal clone starts with zero of either side.
whyPeopleStillPay: Seekers mostly do not pay, so the paying side is owners, agents and developers buying visibility against everyone else buying visibility. They pay because the buyer traffic is already there and nowhere else in India has the same concentration of it outside one or two rivals. That is not a software fee, it is rent on an audience, and no amount of local code produces an audience.
notes: Cloning the search UI takes an afternoon and leaves you with an empty database. The moat is millions of live listings and the brokers and buyers who both show up because the other side already did.
prompt:
Build a local-only "flat hunt tracker" web app. This is a personal shortlist and comparison tool, NOT a listings portal: it never scrapes or crawls any property site.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js with the App Router, TypeScript, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind for styling, MapLibre GL with free OpenStreetMap raster tiles for the map. Single process, runs with npm run dev on localhost. No auth, no accounts, no analytics, no telemetry, no external SaaS.

Data model in SQLite: listing (id, title, source_url, source_name, locality, city, lat, lng, rent_or_price, deposit, carpet_area_sqft, bhk, furnishing, floor, posted_by, contact_note, status enum of new/shortlisted/visited/rejected/closed, created_at), visit (id, listing_id, visited_on, notes, rating 1 to 5), followup (id, listing_id, due_on, note, done).

Features that must work:
1. Add Listing form. All fields manual. If the user pastes a URL, store it as a plain link, do not fetch it.
2. Geocode locality plus city through the public Nominatim endpoint, with a 1 request per second rate limit and a descriptive User-Agent, and let the user drag the map pin to correct it. Cache geocode results in SQLite.
3. Duplicate detection on save: warn if an existing listing has the same source_url, or a similar title within 300 metres, and offer merge or keep both.
4. Scoring. User sets weights in a settings page for price, area, commute and their own gut rating. Define one or more "anchor" addresses (office, school) and compute straight line distance to each. Show a normalised 0 to 100 score per listing and sort by it. Be explicit in the UI that distance is as the crow flies, not commute time.
5. Compare view: pick up to 4 listings, show a side by side table including rent per square foot.
6. Map view with colour coded pins by status, click a pin to open the listing.
7. Visits and follow-ups with a simple "due this week" list on the dashboard.
8. CSV import and export of listings, plus a one click SQLite file download for backup.

Explicitly out of scope: scraping, any portal API, email parsing, notifications, multi-user, mobile apps, payments.

Store nothing secret; if any config is needed put it in .env.local and commit .env.example instead. Seed the database with 5 fake listings so the map and scoring are visible on first run. Write a README that states plainly: this tool manages listings you found yourself, it does not find them for you.
